quick.summary: Why a screen that looked finished broke on day one, and five states to design.
quick.takeaway: Empty, loading, error, partial and full. Design all five.

beats.line: My dashboard looked great. On day one, new users saw a blank page. Why?
You designed the full state only. A screen has five.
Empty. Nothing here yet, and what to do first.
Error. What went wrong, and how to recover.
Partial, with only a little data. And full.
Five designs for every screen? That doubles my work.
Small ones. Otherwise the developer invents them for you.
Empty state: no reports yet, with a button to create the first.
Now day one has a way forward.

quiz.question: A new user opens a list screen before adding anything. Which state do they see?
quiz.explanation: With no content yet, the screen shows its empty state, which should say what to do first.

quiz.question: If a designer leaves out the error state, the developer usually has to invent it.
quiz.explanation: Something must appear when things fail, so an undesigned state gets decided during the build.
